verdict: AppLovin's advertising platform nearly doubled in a year — software revenue rose 88% to $576M — powering a $172M profit on $953M of total revenue, even as its own game apps shrank.

kpis.label: Net income
kpis.note: for the whole company, apps included

segments.name: Software Platform
segments.note: Fees from advertisers using AppLovin's AXON ad platform, MAX mediation and Adjust measurement — the business AppLovin kept.

segments.name: Apps
segments.note: In-app purchases and ads inside AppLovin's own mobile games — the business it sold to Tripledot in June 2025.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Product and engineering for the platform and the game studios.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Buying players for the apps, plus selling the platform to advertisers — the biggest running cost in the old two-business model.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and head office.

follow100Note: Rows may not add exactly due to rounding. Interest on AppLovin's debt — $9.51 of every $100 — sits in 'Other expense, net' below the operating line.

takeaways.title: The AXON engine took off
takeaways.text: Software Platform revenue rose 88% year-over-year to $576M as the AXON AI ad engine won bigger advertiser budgets. The platform passed the apps business to become 60% of all revenue.

takeaways.title: Half of revenue became EBITDA
takeaways.text: Adjusted EBITDA was $476M — 50 cents of every revenue dollar — up 83% from $260M a year ago. GAAP profit was $172M after $91M of net interest and other costs and a small tax bill.

takeaways.title: The apps were already fading
takeaways.text: Apps revenue slipped 5% to $377M. AppLovin was steering the company toward the software platform — in June 2025 it sold the apps business to Tripledot Studios.

otherDetail: Interest expense and loss on settlement of debt of $72M — the bill on AppLovin's borrowings — plus $19M of other expense, net: a net -$91M in this step.
footerNote: Figures are as originally reported for Q4 2023 — the quarter as AppLovin reported it at the time, with both businesses in (derived from the FY2023 Form 10-K less the nine months to September 2023 in the Q3 2023 Form 10-Q). Every later quarter on this page is shown on the continuing-operations basis AppLovin adopted after selling its apps business in June 2025, with the apps folded into the 'other' step. No SEC filing restates Q4 2023 on that basis — the restated quarterly statements begin with the 2024 quarters, and full-year 2023 continuing revenue of $1,842M appears only as an annual total in the FY2025 Form 10-K — so this quarter keeps the apps as their own revenue line instead.
